title: Root-lattice adjoint torus and its action on root lines
statement: Let $A$ be a nonzero commutative ring, and let $(G,T=D_A(M))$ be a split realization of a finite reduced root datum $(M,\Phi,M^\vee,\Phi^\vee)$, with the notions of [def-sfb-pinned-split-root-realization] and pinning and base forgotten. Let $Q=\mathbf Z\Phi\subseteq M$ be the subgroup generated by the roots. The centre $Z(G)$, meaning the subgroup functor of points commuting with all points after every algebra extension, is $D_A(M/Q)\subseteq D_A(M)$, and the fppf sheaf quotient $T/Z(G)$ is $D_A(Q)$ [def-sfb-ring-diagonalizable-group]. Here a fppf sheaf quotient is the sheafification of the pointwise quotient for flat finitely presented jointly surjective covers. Conjugation by $T$ on $G$ descends to an action of $D_A(Q)$ by $A$-group-scheme automorphisms. For every commutative $A$-algebra $B$, $t\in D_A(Q)(B)$ corresponds to a homomorphism $Q\to B^\times$; its automorphism $c_t$ fixes $T_B$ pointwise and acts on the base-changed root line $\mathfrak g_{\alpha,B}$ by multiplication by $t(\alpha)$ for every $\alpha\in\Phi$. It thus preserves the root labels and induces the identity constant lattice map on $T_B$. The statements commute with arbitrary base change, include $Q=0$ and allow nonreduced and disconnected rings.

source.place: Corollary 3.3.6(1), printed p.101; Example 5.1.7, p.138; proof of Corollary 6.1.15, p.196, paragraph on the descended conjugation action and root characters. Read online; local PDF WANTED. No Stacks tag states this reductive-group structural theorem.

proof.text: A central section of $G$ commutes with $T$ after every scalar extension, so [lem-sfb-split-torus-self-centralizer-arbitrary-base] places it in $T$. The adjoint-action kernel statement [lem-sfb-adjoint-action-kernel-is-centre] then identifies the centre inside $T$ with the kernel of the restricted $T$-action on $\operatorname{Lie}(G)$. Both identifications are scheme-theoretic and survive arbitrary base change, so this reduction applies to every $A$-algebra $B$.

In the pinned split realization, the tangent module is the direct sum of $\operatorname{Lie}(T)$ and the free rank-one root lines $\mathfrak g_\alpha$. For $t\in T(B)$, the defining weight equation gives $\operatorname{Ad}(t)(v)=\chi_\alpha(t)v$ on $B\otimes_A\mathfrak g_\alpha$, while $T$ acts trivially on $\operatorname{Lie}(T)$. Since each root line has a basis and the sum is direct, the restricted adjoint action is the identity exactly when $\chi_\alpha(t)=1$ for every $\alpha\in\Phi$; this remains true over nonreduced $B$ and when $\Phi$ is empty.

source.place: Corollary 3.3.6(1), printed p.101; root-character calculation in the proof of Theorem 3.3.4

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-relative-diagonalizable-character-duality] to the inclusion $D_A(M/Q)=D_A(M/\mathbf Z\Phi)\hookrightarrow D_A(M)$: its quotient clause says that the fppf sheaf quotient of $D_A(M)$ by this subgroup is $D_A(Q)$. The same theorem identifies this subgroup with the common kernel of the characters $(\chi_\alpha)_{\alpha\in\Phi}$, and says all these descriptions commute with arbitrary base change. Combining with steps 1 and 2 gives $Z(G)=D_A(M/Q)$ and $T/Z(G)=D_A(Q)$ scheme-theoretically, including $Q=0$.

Because $Z(G)$ is central, conjugation by $T$ is constant on its cosets and therefore descends fppf-locally, then uniquely as a sheaf action, to $D_A(Q)=T/Z(G)$. For a $B$-point $t$ represented by the character $Q\to B^\times$, the defining weight equation on each root line is multiplication by $t(\alpha)$, and the torus summand is fixed pointwise. Thus the descended automorphism fixes $T_B$, preserves every root label and has the asserted scalar on $\mathfrak g_{\alpha,B}$. The quotient description, the action and these formulas are all obtained after arbitrary base change, so the disconnected, nonreduced and empty-root cases are included.

from.place: Supporting input for Theorem 6.1.17: root-lattice adjoint torus and its action on root lines; the item realizes the centre/quotient and descended conjugation formulas described in Conrad Corollary 3.3.6(1), Example 5.1.7 and the proof of Corollary 6.1.15.

split_report.summary: Split the arbitrary-base adjoint-torus statement into four proof steps. The first uses two new statement-only arbitrary-base structural inputs (self-centrality of a split maximal torus and the adjoint-action kernel description); the second expands the root-line calculation directly from the pinned-realization definition; the third applies the existing diagonalizable-character quotient theorem; and the fourth descends conjugation and records base-change and edge cases. The source statement is unchanged.
split_report.blueprint: The steps realize the supporting root-lattice adjoint-torus input in the proof of Theorem 6.1.17, together with Conrad Corollary 3.3.6(1), Example 5.1.7 and the descended-conjugation paragraph in the proof of Corollary 6.1.15.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q104-c9d59553b (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item (statement unchanged, 4 steps) and both new nodes in full. Conrad's Reductive group schemes has no local copy, so I fetched it read-only from the URL in the nodes and checked these places against its text: Thm 3.3.4 (p.98; Z_G(T)=T used p.101), Cor 3.3.6(1) (p.101, centre = kernel of the T-adjoint action), Prop 3.3.8 (p.102, Z_G = ker Ad_G over any base), Example 2.2.6/Lemma 2.2.4 (pp.64-66), Example 5.1.7 (p.138, Z_G = D(M/Q)) and Cor 6.1.15 (p.196, the (T/Z)-action c_t). Steps: (1) the self-centralizer node puts the centre inside T, and the Z∩T = ker(Ad|T) clause of the adjoint-kernel node identifies it there. (2) The pinned-realization definition really does require Lie(T) ⊕ free rank-one root lines with full-character weights, so trivial restricted Ad is equivalent to χ_α(t)=1 for all α, also over nonreduced B and with Φ empty. (3) The duality node applied to Z^Φ→M gives kernel D(M/Q) and quotient D(M)/D(M/Q)=D(Q), compatible with base change. (4) Conjugation descends through the fppf quotient by centrality, with scalar t(α) on root lines. Small cases: SL_2 gives μ_2 (I checked ker Ad by hand in char 2 with nilpotents), PGL_2 gives a trivial centre, empty Φ gives Q=0. New nodes: C_G(T)=T over arbitrary A (true by Lemma 2.2.4, the field case and the fibral criterion B.3.1), and Z=ker Ad with Z∩T=ker(Ad|T) (exactly Conrad Prop 3.3.8 and Cor 3.3.6(1)). Neither restates the item. Neither duplicates an existing node: the self-centralizer and Ad-kernel nodes generalize the field-only lem-sfb-reductive-torus-self-centralizer and the Noetherian lem-sfb-relative-reductive-centre-weight-kernel; lem-sfb-relative-torus-centralizer-normalizer gives only representability and Lie. Batch-5: def-sfb-pinned-split-root-realization reaches lem-trf-smooth-fpqc-base-descent and the duality node reaches lem-trf-fppf-covering-is-fpqc. Both are general descent/topology facts, outside the trace-formula and Poincaré assumptions and their proofs, so I accepted them. The base item had no proof, so the re-split shortening rule does not apply. No SGA cited. No tool_uses, no fixes.
